key_concept: Each region of the electromagnetic spectrum has a characteristic use set by its frequency and energy: microwaves heat food, UV kills microbes, gamma rays destroy cancer cells and radio waves carry AM/FM signals.
steps: P (Microwave): The frequency of microwaves ($\sim 2.45\,\text{GHz}$ in ovens) makes water molecules in food oscillate, and this produces heat. So P → II (warming the food).
Q (UV rays): UV photons are energetic enough to damage the DNA of bacteria and viruses, so UV lamps are used to sterilise and purify water. So Q → I (purifying water).
R (Gamma rays): Gamma rays have the highest energy (shortest $\lambda$, below about $10^{-12}\,\text{m}$). They are used in radiotherapy to kill cancer cells. So R → IV (treating cancer cells).
S (Radio waves): AM uses about $530\,\text{kHz}$–$1710\,\text{kHz}$ and FM uses about $88$–$108\,\text{MHz}$, both in the radio band. So S → III (AM and FM communication).
The correct matching is P-II, Q-I, R-IV, S-III, which is option (3).
why_not_others: Options (1) and (2) pair microwaves with water purification, but microwaves heat matter rather than sterilise it. Option (4) gives cancer treatment to UV and water purification to radio waves, but radio photons carry far too little energy to kill microbes.
common_trap: Students often mix up UV and gamma rays because both are 'harmful/medical' radiations. UV is for sterilisation and water purification, while gamma rays, being far more penetrating, are for cancer therapy.
time_saving_tip: Fix the most certain pair first: microwave → warming food (P-II). Only options (3) and (4) survive. Then radio → AM/FM (S-III) leaves only option (3).
